f: GML is an open geographic data format.
The format is used for compliance with the EU INSPIRE framework.
HM Land Registry uses GML to provide a standard data structure across GIS and CAD systems.
GML can be converted into other GIS formats.
The required conversion depends on the target GIS or CAD system.
Users may need guidance from their GIS provider for system-specific conversion.
A converted dataset must also use an appropriate projection for the target tool.
Use in Google Maps may require conversion from GML to KML.
QGIS is identified as free software.
QGIS is identified as open-source software.
QGIS can be used to view GML data.
QGIS can convert GML into other formats.
Opening a GML in QGIS starts by adding a vector layer.
The GML file type is selected when browsing for the file.
QGIS conversion uses the layer Save As operation.
ESRI Shapefile is listed as an available conversion target.
MapInfo MIF is listed as an available conversion target.
MapInfo TAB is listed as an available conversion target.
AutoCAD DXF is listed as an available conversion target.
GeoJSON is listed as an available conversion target.
KML is listed as an available conversion target.
HM Land Registry polygon geometry is captured against British National Grid.
Polygon vertices are represented by X and Y coordinate values.
British National Grid is identified as EPSG:27700.
Use in Google or Bing web maps requires reprojection.
Google and Bing use WGS 84 Pseudo-Mercator.
WGS 84 Pseudo-Mercator is identified as EPSG:3857.
QGIS can reproject British National Grid data to other coordinate systems.
Coordinate transformation calculations may introduce positional error.
The guidance warns that BNG-to-WGS84 conversion can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
INSPIRE Index Polygons is described as an open-source dataset.
The dataset was developed to comply with the INSPIRE Directive.
It contains locations of registered freehold property in England and Wales.
It is a subset of the full Index Polygons database.
The data is divided into separate files by local-authority area.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary may appear in both authority files.
An INSPIRE polygon shows the position of a registered property.
An INSPIRE polygon shows only the indicative extent of a registered property.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
The Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relates the polygon to a registered title.
The INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain title information.
Find a Property can provide the title plan associated with an INSPIRE polygon.
The exact extent of a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons.
The individual title plan is required to identify the registered extent.
A registered title has a single title number.
One title can contain several separate polygons.
Each polygon belonging to a title has its own INSPIRE ID.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can indicate that land is not registered.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can also result from leasehold tenure.
Other tenures excluded from the dataset can also explain absence of an INSPIRE ID.
The index map can be searched to check whether land is registered.
Business e-services users can view the full Index Polygon dataset through MapSearch.
MapSearch access to the full Index Polygon dataset is described as free for business e-services users.
INSPIRE polygons and attributes are available under the Open Government Licence.
Reuse under the OGL is free.
Failure to meet OGL conditions automatically ends the granted reuse rights.
Reuse requires an HM Land Registry source attribution.
Reuse of polygon geometry also requires Ordnance Survey attribution.
A link to the dataset conditions should be provided where possible.
New INSPIRE files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
A monthly publication contains data from the previous month.
The current files remain accessible until the next publication.
The files are published in GML format.
A GIS is needed to view the downloaded polygons.
GIS software can store or edit the downloaded data.
GIS software can compare or integrate the polygons with other datasets.
The current download page states a publication date of 5 July 2026.
The current download page offers polygon downloads by local authority.
The live Article 4 direction dataset reports 3,175 directions.
The live dataset reports 102 data providers.
The collector last ran on 31 July 2026.
New data was last found on 31 July 2026.
An Article 4 direction can alter or remove permitted-development rights from a building or area.
A direction may apply to one or more Article 4 direction areas.
Each direction area may have one or more Article 4 direction rules.
The dataset states that it currently contains data from a small group of local planning authorities.
The authorities are being used to develop the Article 4 data specification.
Some records were created by MHCLG and are intended to be replaced by authoritative sources.
The live dataset is licensed under Open Government Licence version 3.0.
The live dataset attribution is Crown copyright and database right 2026.
The live Article 4 direction area dataset reports 7,152 areas.
The live area dataset reports 112 data providers.
The area collector last ran on 31 July 2026.
The area dataset last found new data on 31 July 2026.
The dataset contains information about areas affected by Article 4 directions.
The area data supports development control.
An Article 4 area may require a planning application for work otherwise classed as permitted development.
Some area records were created by MHCLG and are intended to be replaced by authoritative sources.
The area dataset is licensed under Open Government Licence version 3.0.
The area dataset attribution is Crown copyright and database right 2026.
Article 4 publication requires a direction dataset and a direction-area dataset.
CSV is an accepted Article 4 publication format.
GeoJSON is an accepted Article 4 publication format.
GML is an accepted Article 4 publication format.
GeoPackage is an accepted Article 4 publication format.
The datasets can be uploaded to a single URL.
The datasets can be served through an OGC Web Feature Service.
The datasets can be served through an ArcGIS API.
Uppercase field-name characters are converted to lowercase.
The direction dataset needs at least one row per direction.
A direction reference must be unique within the provider dataset.
A direction reference must remain unchanged when the dataset is updated.
A provider without an existing identifier must create one.
The name field records the official direction name.
document-url identifies the authoritative order or notice.
documentation-url identifies the webpage introducing the document.
The documentation webpage must include a short description.
Each direction must have a unique documentation URL.
A unique anchor fragment may distinguish records sharing a webpage.
end-date remains blank while the direction is active.
entry-date records when the entity was last updated.
For a never-updated entity, entry-date equals start-date.
The area dataset needs at least one row per area.
An area reference must be unique within the provider dataset.
An area reference must remain stable across updates.
Area geometry is supplied as a polygon or multipolygon.
CSV geometry is encoded as Well-Known Text.
GeoJSON, GML and GeoPackage use their native geometry encodings.
UPRN is applicable when the geometry represents a building boundary.
UPRN and address-text must be supplied together when either is used.
article-4-direction links an area to its direction reference.
Multiple withdrawn permitted-development rights are separated by semicolons.
Only rights present in the Planning Data permitted-development-right dataset should be used.
The data webpage should be hosted on the planning authority's official website.
The webpage must link to the data endpoint.
The webpage must summarise what the data covers.
The webpage must state that the data is provided under the Open Government Licence.
The 1m composite DTM covers approximately 99% of England.
The composite spatial resolution is 1 metre.
The product is a raster elevation model.
The DTM uses the last or only laser pulse return.
Surface objects are removed from the DSM to create the terrain model.
The surface-removal workflow uses bespoke algorithms.
The surface-removal workflow also uses manual editing.
The resulting DTM represents the terrain surface rather than buildings and vegetation.
The composite was produced by the Environment Agency in 2022.
The composite uses surveys from the Time Stamped archive.
The composite uses National LIDAR Programme surveys.
The input surveys were merged and resampled.
The merging process is intended to provide the best possible coverage.
Where surveys repeat, the newest survey is selected.
Where surveys repeat, the best-resolution survey is selected.
The composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000.
The composite contains surveys through 2 April 2022.
Metadata index catalogues identify the contributing survey for a location.
Download rasters are supplied as GeoTIFF.
Download rasters are organised into 5 km tiles.
The 5 km tiles are aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevation values are presented in metres.
The vertical reference is Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
Input surveys have a vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 cm RMSE.
The metadata states that there are no public access constraints.
Use is subject to the Open Government Licence.
The listed attribution is Environment Agency copyright and/or database right 2022.
LIDAR is described as an airborne mapping technique.
LIDAR uses a laser to measure terrain and surface-object heights.
The technique makes hundreds of thousands of measurements per second.
Environment Agency LIDAR products can have spatial resolutions from 25 cm to 2 m.
The coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The dataset geographic extent begins at latitude 49.943.
The dataset geographic extent ends at latitude 55.816.
The dataset geographic extent begins at longitude -6.236.
The dataset geographic extent ends at longitude 2.072.
A WMS service is listed for the 1m DTM.
A WMS service is listed for the metadata survey index catalogues.
A WFS service is listed for the metadata survey index catalogues.
A WCS service is listed for the 1m DTM.
A WMTS service is listed for the 1m DTM.
An OGC API Features service is listed.
The metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
The metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
The 2m composite DTM is listed as a related dataset.
The 10m composite DTM is listed as a related dataset.
The 1m composite DSM is listed as a related dataset.
WCS provides raw coverage pixel values such as elevation.
WCS GeoTIFF output uses a numeric NoData value of -3.4028235e+38.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset.
OS Terrain 50 provides a digital terrain model of Great Britain.
The DTM removes protruding features such as buildings and trees.
OS Terrain 50 is the lower-resolution member of the OS Terrain product family.
It is designed for landscape visualisation and large-area analysis.
OS Terrain 50 is an Open Data product.
It is free to view, download and use for commercial, educational and personal purposes.
The product is published as both grid and contour data.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
Tiled supplies use 10 km by 10 km tiles.
A tile is identified by the National Grid reference of its south-west corner.
Grid posts have regular 50 m spacing.
Standard contour polylines use a 10 m interval.
Contour data includes mean high water boundaries.
Contour data includes mean low water boundaries.
Grid data is available as ASCII grid.
Grid data is available as GML 3.2.1.
The GML supply uses Simple Features Profile level 0.
Contour data is available as GML 3.2.1.
Contour data is available as Esri Shapefile.
Contour data is available as GeoPackage.
Contour data is available as vector tiles in MBTiles.
Grid and contour supplies are delivered separately.
Tiled data is supplied in compressed folders.
Online download is available without registration.
ASCII, GML and Shapefile supplies are available as a full Great Britain tile set.
The full tiled product contains 2,858 tiles.
The tiled supply is arranged into 55 folders.
Each folder represents a 100 km National Grid square.
GeoPackage is supplied as a single national flat file.
Vector tiles are supplied as a single national flat file.
The compressed national supply is not encrypted.
A full national compressed grid supply is approximately 157 MB.
The data is maintained through annual full-tile resupply.
OS Terrain 50 is supplied annually in July.
ASCII grid is readable by most standard GIS software without translation.
The companion GML carries metadata such as location, spacing and vertical reference.
ASCII data is represented as a raster grid.
Each height value is calculated from the centre of a pixel.
The map-header origin represents the north-west corner of the tile.
Rows are ordered from west to east.
Each pixel is 50 m by 50 m.
Successive rows proceed southward at 50 m intervals.
Grid heights are supplied to the nearest 0.1 m.
The .asc file stores the Esri ASCII grid.
The .gml file allows the grid to be loaded as GML.
The .prj file stores the spatial reference in Esri format.
The .asc.aux.xml file supplies default Esri styling parameters.
A Metadata_<tile>.xml file provides tile metadata such as flying date.
The ASCII header specifies a cell size of 50.
Contour GML is supplied in GML version 3.2.1.
Using contour GML requires familiarity with XML and XML schemas.
Each contour tile includes a <tile>.gml data file.
Each contour tile includes a Metadata_<tile>.xml file.
Spot heights are generated using an automated selection process.
The process selects the highest mass point inside each closed contour.
A spot height equal to its surrounding contour height is removed.
A spot height may be lower than a surrounding contour in a genuine depression.
Spot-height Z values are rounded to zero decimal places.
The national contour vector-tile supply is contained in one MBTiles file.
The vector-tile set is described as lightweight.
The vector-tile set is designed for efficient, fast rendering.
The vector-tile set provides high-resolution data.
The vector-tile set is designed for seamless zooming.
The vector-tile data is supplied in Web Mercator.
Terrain contour layers and attributes are not mapped at zoom levels 0 to 8.
The listed terrain layers and attributes are mapped at zoom levels 9 through 14.
The schema includes a contour_line layer.
The schema includes a spot_height layer.
The schema includes a land_water_boundary layer.
OS Terrain 50 XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
Metadata is supplied for national product sets.
Metadata is also supplied per tile.
The XML includes comments explaining tag meanings.
Metadata distinguishes grid DTM from vector contours.
Metadata records the 10 km National Grid tile reference.
The metadata topic category is elevation.
An XSLT stylesheet is supplied for viewing XML as HTML.
The Esri auxiliary XML stores minimum, maximum, mean and standard-deviation height statistics.
The same styling statistics are supplied for every tile.
The statistics support consistent colour ramps across adjacent tiles.
Default styling can be disabled by removing the auxiliary XML.
Default styling can also be changed by adjusting minimum and maximum values.
